_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY — placeholders. Copy to secrets.<env>.json (git-ignored), fill real values there. Never commit real secrets. See README.md → 'Environments' and 'Secrets to replace for production'.
_comment_environment: 'environment' is LOAD-BEARING: it yields the env code (development->dev, production->prod) that prefixes every project-global GCP id and names the per-environment state bucket. Teardown destroys the WORKLOAD layer only for EVERY environment (the DNS zone + state bucket are always preserved — they cost almost nothing to keep); a non-production 'teardown --purge' ALSO destroys the DNS zone + state bucket + sweeps secrets (production forbids --purge). Run 'spacestroker-deploy validate' to see every derived id.
_comment_clusterUrl: GeneralSettings:Token:ClusterUrl is a SECRET, not appConfig: the RPC provider's api-key rides in the URL's query string, and appConfig entries become plaintext Cloud Run env vars. Devnet form: https://devnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=... The FALLBACK below is a plain public endpoint with no key, so it stays in appConfig.
_comment_analytics: GA4: ONE measurement id serves BOTH properties — the app reads VUE_APP_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and the landing page reads PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID, so set them to the SAME G-XXXXXXXXXX. That is what keeps the LP -> app hop a single session (same registrable domain, shared _ga cookie), so a bet is attributed to the campaign that brought the visitor. Both live in frontBuild because the deploy tool writes that same block into BOTH repo builds and each toolchain only exposes its own prefix (Vue CLI: VUE_APP_*, Astro/Vite: PUBLIC_*). EMPTY = analytics never loads: no script, no cookie, no consent banner — keep them empty in secrets.development.json so dev never reports into the production property. The id is public in the page source, so it is config rather than a credential, but still never commit a real one.
